units.text: INT. CHURCH BELL TOWER - DAY
Snow drifts through the broken louvres and settles on the great bronze bell like flour on a baker's arm.
The wooden stair groans below.
The air smells of pigeon and old rope.
SERGEANT MAGNUS HADLEY, 40s, a face scoured by wind, crouches at the north louvre with binoculars.
PRIVATE QUIGG, 19, freckled, hugs a machine gun.
PRIVATE NASRIN KHALIL, 20s, a field radio strapped to her back, picks at a frozen knot.
CORPORAL TOMASZ WIERZBICKI, 30s, sits against the wall, bandaging his own hand.
They're moving in the orchard.
units.name: QUIGG

units.text: Count.
units.name: HADLEY

units.text: Nine? Ten --
units.name: NASRIN

units.text: Twelve. I said twelve.
units.name: QUIGG

units.text: Twelve, nine, who cares, we're up a steeple.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: Quiet. Both of you.
units.name: HADLEY

units.text: A footstep on the stair.
Slow.
Four rifles swing.
MOTHER AGATHE, 70s, a black habit and a snow-crusted shawl, climbs into the loft carrying a kettle.
She is breathing hard and not remotely afraid.
You have been in my bell tower since Tuesday. I thought you might want tea.
units.name: MOTHER AGATHE

units.text: Mother, you can't be up here --
units.name: NASRIN

units.text: Is it safe? Did you check it?
units.name: QUIGG

units.text: She's a nun, she's not going to poison us.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: Not before the second cup.
units.name: MOTHER AGATHE

units.text: Hadley lowers the binoculars.
For the first time all day, he laughs.
